thread:
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT: auth-service: unusual token reuse + external log indexing detected. Severity: P1. Possible sensitive lines (session tokens) leaked to third-party indexer. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth-leak

elena: taking this — oncall SRE. Adding folks: @omar @jia @kevin @mia-cs @legal.

omar: confirming. what is the scope? any customer-facing outages?

jia: quick scan of auth logs (last 2h) shows ~1200 requests with same session token across 3 IPs. Most from staging-ish UA strings. Query: `kubectl logs -n prod auth-0 | grep \"session_id=\" | jq -r .session | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 20`

jia: also found a suspicious S3 path pushed to our log-forwarder: `s3://redwood-prod-logs/edge/2026-03-17/part-00042.json` containing unredacted headers. Indexer endpoint: https://indexer.external/search?id=acct-77

kevin: if logs were forwarded to that external indexer, we should block egress first. I can push a security-group change and temporary NACL deny for the indexer IP range.

elena: do that now — block egress for the piggybacked forwarder host group. Kevin, call the exact SG change.

kevin: running:
```
# revoke egress to external indexer
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0abc12345 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 52.23.45.0/24
# apply DENY NACL on prod-subnet-4 for that range
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-0def6789 --rule-number 200 --protocol 6 --rule-action deny --egress true --cidr-block 52.23.45.0/24
```
kevin: done. egress blocked, confirmed tcp 443 handshake fails from forwarder host.

jia: starting a targeted scrub to remove the leaked objects from the forwarding bucket and then request takedown from indexer. Running removal job against s3 prefix: `aws s3 rm s3://redwood-prod-logs/edge/2026-03-17/part-00042.json`

omar: please also rotate any service principals with access to that bucket and the forwarder. Which service accounts?@jia?

jia: service principal `svc-log-forwarder` and `svc-indexer-sync` appear in the bucket policy. I'll initiate key rotation for both. Plan: rotate keys, deploy updated creds to forwarder, remove old keys, redeploy. Estimated 25-40m.

elena: priority: (1) block egress (done), (2) remove leaked object (jia), (3) rotate keys (jia), (4) notify CS/legal if customer impact.

mia-cs: do we know impacted customers yet? customers should be proactively notified only if any PII or customer tokens leaked. I can prepare a brief once scope confirmed.

jia: quick grep shows tokens that map to internal staging and two small customers (customer ids: cust-842, cust-918) used in integration tests. I do not yet see production customer traffic. Could still be some internal developer API keys.

legal: copy — hold off public disclosure until we confirm what data types leaked. If PII/credentials in the leak, we'll need the notification cadence and timeline.

kevin: rotation commands: 
```
# generate new key
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-log-forwarder
# update k8s secret (example)
kubectl -n infra set secret generic forwarder-creds --from-literal=AKID=NEW --from-literal=SECRET=NEWSECRET
# rollout
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/log-forwarder
```
kevin: I'll coordinate with infra CI to avoid restarts during burst hours. Doing now.

jia: scrub job removed the offending objects from s3 and invalidated the indexer link (file removed). Submitted takedown request to indexer support with proof-of-ownership: https://indexer.external/support/tickets/12487 (they acknowledged).

omar: any evidence of keys being exfiltrated beyond the object lines?

jia: not seeing outbound pushes besides the forwarding job. No other services talked to that indexer IP. Logs show a cron job from `svc-log-forwarder` pushed the file at 14:11 UTC.

elena: timeline so far: 14:11 file push -> 14:22 pager, 14:25 egress block, 14:28 scrub remove, 14:35 rotation started, 14:58 rotation complete and forwarder restarted with new creds.

mia-cs: prepping customer message draft for cust-842 and cust-918. Will wait for legal sign-off.

legal: draft ack: "We detected a limited set of internal logs that included token-like strings. We have revoked the implicated keys, removed the logs from our storage, and requested takedown from the third-party indexer. We are investigating potential impact and will follow up within 72 hours." I'll review final copy.

elena: operational ask: create follow-up tasks: postmortem, confirm no other leaked prefixes, tighten bucket policies to require KMS and deny public indexing, rotate any long-lived tokens, add monitoring alert for high token reuse.

kevin: created a short runbook PR with tighter S3 bucket policy and an alert rule for token reuse spike. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/4532

omar: handoff — SRE team will monitor for 6 hours. If no further evidence, we'll move to P2 and schedule a full postmortem.

mia-cs: once legal signs, I'll send both customers a notification and offer remediation help.

elena: thanks team. Logged incident ticket INC-2026-0317-87 and moving thread to incidents channel for postmortem. If anyone sees new activity, ping me directly. :white_check_mark:
